metadata.title: What Makes School Systems Perform? Seeing School Systems through the Prism of PISA 2000

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD synthesis report summarizes cross-national findings from PISA 2000 and a multilateral qualitative framework study across six reference countries (Canada, England, Finland, France, Netherlands, Sweden). It does not provide an analysis-ready student micro-dataset, nor does it specify any sampling/replicate weight variables or how they would be applied in estimation. For PISA-based achievement comparisons, analysts using the OECD PISA database would typically apply the complex survey design weights and combine plausible values using standard PISA procedures; however, this report itself does not document those technical steps. Therefore, no weight variable name can be extracted from the text, and the report should be treated as a policy synthesis rather than a re-estimation of PISA micro-data.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: The report is a qualitative/policy synthesis that does not conduct a student-level statistical re-analysis with a documented missing-data strategy. While it references PISA 2000 results (including mean scores and differences) and discusses system-level factors, it does not specify how missing responses or nonresponse were handled in any empirical model estimated within this document. As a result, missing-data handling is not reported for the purposes of this synthesis.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The report does not define an analytic student-level subsample. Instead, it synthesizes PISA 2000 results for six reference countries (Canada, England, Finland, France, Netherlands, Sweden) and summarizes findings from a multilateral qualitative study coordinated by the German Institute for International Educational Research. For the PISA-referenced comparisons shown (e.g., Table 1 on native-born vs foreign-born performance), the report cites the OECD PISA database but does not specify any additional inclusion/exclusion criteria or analytic filtering steps.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD report synthesizes what drives school system performance by “seeing school systems through the prism of PISA 2000.” It does not estimate predictive models; instead, it summarizes cross-national patterns and policy features across six reference countries (Canada, England, Finland, France, Netherlands, Sweden) and links them to themes such as reform and innovation, devolution of responsibilities, system monitoring, support systems, standards, classroom organization, integration of non-native students, and coping with under-achievement. The report uses PISA 2000 as an anchor for comparative performance and equity discussions, including mean score differences for native-born versus foreign-born students (Table 1), while also drawing on a multilateral qualitative analytical framework (Annex A) to structure country evidence. Because it is a synthesis, it does not report model-based metrics (e.g., AUC/RMSE) or document plausible-value combination or missing-data procedures for any re-estimation. Consequently, the findings are best interpreted as policy-relevant correlational/interpretive insights rather than causal or model-evaluated effects.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This document is a policy synthesis/report that summarizes PISA 2000 results and qualitative country evidence rather than conducting an original student-level empirical ML analysis. As a result, there is no extractable analytic sample size, no documented survey-weight or replicate-weight application, no explicit plausible-value handling procedure for an estimated model, and no missing-data handling strategy tied to an estimation procedure. The absence of ML techniques and structured predictive outcomes is therefore due to the report’s design as a synthesis rather than a methodological transparency gap for an ML pipeline.
